scope_note: This repository is a monorepo containing the shadcn/ui CLI, its docs/demo site, and framework-fixture/template trees used only to test the CLI's project scaffolding. This run graded apps/v4 (the real Next.js application: registry/new-york-v4 component source, blocks, docs pages, and the app/globals.css token layer) and excluded packages/shadcn/test/fixtures/** and templates/** as CLI test fixtures and starter scaffolds, not consuming application code. Denominators below (e.g. 1,230 files) are apps/v4 only.

tier-integrity.note: 26 of 1,230 scanned .tsx files (2.1%) reach past the semantic color layer for a raw Tailwind palette utility (neutral-*, gray-*, blue-*) where a semantic token already covers the case. The largest cluster is a `.dialog-ring` utility (globals.css:456) and its one caller (welcome-dialog.tsx:41,43), both hardcoding `neutral-900`/`neutral-950`/`neutral-200` instead of the `--popover`/`--border`/`--ring` tokens every other dialog in the registry uses. mobile-nav.tsx uses `bg-blue-500` for a "New" indicator dot with no semantic equivalent token. tailwind-indicator.tsx is a dev-only breakpoint overlay (never renders in production) using `bg-gray-800`. 2.1% falls in the >0%-to-5% band.

leakage.note: A targeted manual scan (not an exhaustive automated pass) of apps/v4 for hardcoded hex/rgb/oklch colors and bracket-arbitrary dimensions. No hardcoded hex or oklch colors were found anywhere in the graded surface outside of legitimate exemptions (fixed SVG brand-logo fills, and CSS attribute selectors matching third-party Recharts inline markup like [stroke='#ccc'] -- these target markup the app doesn't control, not a design decision, so they aren't graded as leaks). All findings are dimension leaks.

coverage.note: 9 of 11 categories present. color, typography, space, size, radius, border, elevation, motion and breakpoint all resolve to a real, named CSS custom property -- either a project token in globals.css, or one of Tailwind v4's own default-theme tokens the project imports via `@import "tailwindcss"` and never overrides (verified against tailwindcss@4.3.3's theme.css: --spacing, --shadow-*, --ease-*, --animate-*, --default-transition-duration, --breakpoint-* all exist there). z-index and opacity do not: Tailwind v4 has no `--z-*` or `--opacity-*` theme scale -- `z-50` and `opacity-50` compile straight to fixed values with no underlying variable for a component author to reach for instead. 9/11 falls in the 8-10 attention band.

mode-completeness.note: Diffed every '--' declaration in ':root' (light, line 99) against '.dark' (line 143): all 34 color-bearing tokens (background, foreground, card, popover, primary, secondary, muted, accent, destructive, border, input, ring, chart-1..5, sidebar and its 7 variants, surface, code and its 3 variants, selection and its foreground) are redefined in both blocks with zero gaps. The one token present in ':root' and absent from '.dark' is '--radius' (globals.css:100) -- a corner-radius value, not a themed appearance token, and .dark applies as an additional class alongside :root rather than replacing it, so --radius correctly falls through unchanged. It is excluded from the gap count as a judgment call: mode-completeness as defined checks for a token whose fallback 'ships wrong', and a shared corner radius across light and dark is the correct, intended behavior, not a bug. references/vitals.md scopes mode-completeness to tokens whose meaning is appearance-dependent -- color, elevation, and anything else whose correct value changes with the mode -- and puts geometry, spacing, typography metrics and timing out of scope by default, since a token like --radius can legitimately hold one value across every mode.

naming-coherence.note: Every design token in the graded layer follows one grammar: a kebab-case role name, optionally suffixed '-foreground' for the on-color text that pairs with it (--card / --card-foreground, --popover / --popover-foreground, --sidebar-accent / --sidebar-accent-foreground, and so on across all 34 color tokens). No second grammar or legacy family was found in the token source. Component-internal CSS custom properties used to implement specific utilities (--scroll-fade-*, --shimmer-* in packages/shadcn/src/tailwind.css) were not counted -- they are implementation state for one utility class, not entries in the design-token layer this run grades.

single-source.note: The default chart palette (--chart-1 through --chart-5, resolving to var(--color-blue-300) through var(--color-blue-800)) is declared independently in four places: the project default in globals.css:120, and three of the four theme-preset blocks in legacy-themes.css (.theme-default:3, .theme-scaled:77, .theme-blue:168 -- .theme-mono intentionally overrides with its own stone-based values, which is correct variant behavior, not drift). All four sites currently agree exactly. Nothing stops a future edit to the default palette in one site from silently leaving the other three behind.

orphans.note: Checked all ~53 tokens declared in apps/v4/app/globals.css for at least one reference elsewhere in apps/v4 (as a generated Tailwind utility class -- bg-surface, text-code-number -- or a raw var(--x)). Every token resolved to real usage, including ones that looked orphaned on a first pass: --code-highlight/--code-number are consumed by the rehype-pretty-code styling in globals.css itself (lines 365, 372, 426), --selection/--selection-foreground back the global '::selection' rule (globals.css:196), and --breakpoint-3xl/--breakpoint-4xl are used as Tailwind variants (3xl:, 4xl:) in 17 and 4 files respectively. No orphaned token found; grade is pass, not blocked, because the check was actually run to completion.

enforcement.note: No lint rule or CI gate in this repository reads the token layer. apps/v4/eslint.config.mjs runs eslint-config-next plus typescript-eslint, scoped to type-import style and React hooks correctness -- nothing about colors, spacing, or bracket-arbitrary literals. There is no stylelint config anywhere in the repository (grep found none outside CLI test fixtures, which scaffold OTHER people's projects and aren't this repo's own enforcement). .github/workflows/code-check.yml runs pnpm lint / format:check / typecheck; .github/workflows/validate-registries.yml checks registry namespace collisions, not token usage. 0 qualifying rules found, so per the vital's own grading this is blocked rather than failed: with nothing in place, there is nothing to verify as protecting the system.
